result.title: Algorithmic Monoculture in Machine Learning-based Site-Specific Fertilizer Recommendation
result.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Economics for Machine Learning (EconML)
result.summary: Machine learning recommendations are often evaluated one model at a time, despite deployment across interconnected decision makers. For continuous NPK fertilizer prescriptions, correlated errors can aggregate across farms and generate systemic costs. A model of shared and farm-specific recommendation errors links expected social loss to model adoption shares; the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index characterizes concentration effects when common model errors are independent and predictive risks are equal. A covariance-generalized formulation captures the dependence between model families. A two-model threshold characterizes when privately optimal monoculture is socially dominated, and a convex portfolio rule limits average private predictive regret. Nine model families across five Moroccan cereal systems provide a benchmark-based calibration. Under illustrative parameters and a 10% regret cap, accuracy-constrained diversification lowers modeled social loss in all five systems by 10.89-41.53% (mean 19.41%). Uniform allocation reduces modeled loss in this setting, but breaches the regret cap in every crop. Correlation sensitivity shows that highly dependent model errors attenuate the benefits of diversification. These counterfactual outcomes are not estimates of agronomic or monetary welfare; the framework identifies adoption architecture and error dependence as ecosystem-level evaluation variables.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建共享与农场特异的推荐误差模型，用 HHI 及协方差推广刻画多模型采纳集中度，给出私利最优单一化被社会最优超越的双模型阈值与凸组合配置规则，并在五个摩洛哥种植体系的九个模型族上做基准校准。
